name: rpk-redpanda skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the rpk-redpanda skill adds value over the published rpk reference for node-level commands: rpk redpanda start, stop, mode, check, tune, config, and rpk iotune, plus broker decommission. Fact cases are sampled at even intervals through the pre-thin skill (SKILL.md and its references) or targeted at claims expected to be missing from the docs, chosen from the skill and the public rpk source at v26.2.2 without checking the published docs. Behavioral cases grade the outcome of a task run against a mocked shell: a production broker whose redpanda.yaml still has developer mode on, a broker stopped for a reboot, a decommission that would leave fewer brokers than the replication factor, and production prep of an Azure VM.

test_cases.query: On my MacBook I installed rpk with Homebrew and tried `rpk redpanda tune list` and `rpk iotune` so I could prepare a broker VM, but rpk says unknown command for both. Is my rpk install broken? How do I run these?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda start, stop, mode, check, tune, and config, and rpk iotune, are compiled only into Linux builds of rpk (Go build tag linux); the macOS build registers only the hidden admin subtree under rpk redpanda. They act on the local machine, so they run on the Linux broker node itself. A model tends to suggest reinstalling or upgrading rpk.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/redpanda_darwin.go (registers only admin), src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/redpanda.go and src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/iotune/iotune.go (//go:build linux)
rpk v26.2.5 darwin/arm64: `rpk redpanda tune list` and `rpk iotune` print unknown command

invariants.name: linux_only_run_on_node
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the install is broken or outdated and reinstalling or upgrading rpk on macOS fixes it, or that a profile, flag, or -X option lets the macOS rpk run these commands against the VM. PASSES if it says these commands are included only in the Linux build of rpk, so the macOS build does not have them, and they must be run with rpk on the Linux broker node itself (for example over SSH).

test_cases.query: When I run `rpk redpanda stop` with no flags on a busy Linux broker, what does rpk actually send to the Redpanda process, and how long can it take before the process is killed outright?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda stop sends SIGINT, waits --timeout (default 5s), then sends SIGTERM, waits again, then sends SIGKILL. With defaults the process can be SIGKILLed about 10 seconds after the stop starts. A model tends to describe a single SIGTERM or a systemd-style stop.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/stop.go (signalAndWait over SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGKILL; --timeout default 5s)

invariants.name: escalation_and_timing
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer gives a different order than SIGINT, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, or says rpk waits a total of 5 seconds before SIGKILL, or says it never sends SIGKILL. PASSES if it says rpk sends SIGINT, waits the timeout (5 seconds by default), sends SIGTERM, waits the timeout again, and then sends SIGKILL, so with defaults the process can be killed about 10 seconds after stop begins, and that --timeout changes the wait after each signal.

test_cases.query: Last month I tried `rpk redpanda start --mode dev-container` on one of our Linux hosts. Since then I've only started Redpanda there with plain `rpk redpanda start`, no flags. Is Redpanda on that host running with any of the dev-container settings today?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda start writes its changes into redpanda.yaml before launching, and --mode dev-container sets redpanda.developer_mode: true (plus bundled cluster properties). On every later start, when developer_mode is true and no --mode is given, rpk applies dev-container mode again, including --unsafe-bypass-fsync, --overprovisioned, and --check=false. A model tends to say a --mode flag applies only to that run.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/start.go (developer_mode true with no --mode selects "dev-container"; setContainerModeFlags; setContainerModeCfgFields; y.Write before launch)

invariants.name: dev_mode_persists
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says plain starts run with normal production settings, or that --mode dev-container affected only that one run. PASSES if it says yes: the dev-container start saved developer_mode: true in redpanda.yaml, and rpk redpanda start applies dev-container mode (including bypassing fsync) whenever developer_mode is true and no --mode is given, so the host is still running that way until developer mode is turned off, for example with rpk redpanda mode production.

test_cases.query: On a freshly installed Linux broker, `sudo rpk redpanda tune all` finishes, but its results table shows APPLIED false and ENABLED false for every tuner. What do I do so the tuners actually run?
test_cases.why: Each tuner runs only when its rpk.tune_* key in redpanda.yaml is true, and a fresh install has them off. rpk redpanda mode production turns on the recommended set; individual tuners can be turned on with rpk redpanda config set rpk.tune_<name> true. Then rerun tune all.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/tune/tune.go (skips tuners not enabled; 'All tuners were disabled' message), src/go/rpk/pkg/config/config.go (setProdMode)

invariants.name: enable_via_mode_or_keys
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer blames missing root, a kernel or cloud limitation, or tells the user to add a --force-style flag, without saying the tuners are disabled in redpanda.yaml. PASSES if it says the tuners are disabled in the node's redpanda.yaml (rpk.tune_* keys) and that running rpk redpanda mode production enables the recommended set (or rpk.tune_<name> can be set to true individually), then rerunning tune all applies them.

test_cases.query: I ran `sudo rpk iotune` with its default options on a Linux broker. Do I now need to pass the results to `rpk redpanda start` or reference them in redpanda.yaml for Redpanda to use them?
test_cases.why: rpk iotune writes /etc/redpanda/io-config.yaml by default, and rpk redpanda start looks for io-config.yaml in the directory of the redpanda.yaml it loads and passes it to Redpanda automatically. No flag or config key is needed.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/iotune/iotune.go (--out default: io-config.yaml beside the default redpanda.yaml), src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/start.go (buildRedpandaFlags uses rp.GetIOConfigPath when present), src/go/rpk/pkg/redpanda/paths.go

invariants.name: picked_up_automatically
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the user must pass --io-properties-file, set a redpanda.yaml key, or copy the file somewhere else for Redpanda to use it. PASSES if it says nothing more is needed: iotune wrote /etc/redpanda/io-config.yaml next to redpanda.yaml, and rpk redpanda start picks up io-config.yaml from that directory automatically.

test_cases.query: Our redpanda.yaml sets rpk.well_known_io to 'aws:i3en.xlarge:default'. On one broker I also want to use a measured file, so I start it with `rpk redpanda start --io-properties-file /etc/redpanda/io-measured.yaml`. Which I/O settings does Redpanda use?
test_cases.why: rpk refuses the combination: well_known_io (flag or rpk.well_known_io) and --io-properties or --io-properties-file can't be set at the same time, and start exits with an error. A model tends to say the explicit flag wins.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/start.go (buildRedpandaFlags: "--well-known-io or (rpk.well_known_io) and --io-properties (or --io-properties-file) can't be set at the same time")

invariants.name: start_fails
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the --io-properties-file flag wins, or that rpk.well_known_io wins, or that they are merged. PASSES if it says rpk redpanda start refuses to start with an error because rpk.well_known_io and --io-properties-file can't be set together, and the user must remove rpk.well_known_io on that broker (or drop the flag).

test_cases.query: The host for broker 4 in our self-managed Redpanda cluster died and isn't coming back. How do I decommission broker 4 with rpk when that broker isn't running?
test_cases.why: rpk cluster brokers decommission first checks the broker list and the target's version, and exits when the version is unknown (the node is offline). --skip-liveness-check skips those client-side checks and sends the request; --force is a hidden, deprecated alias.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/cluster/brokers/decommission.go ("version for broker %d is unknown, is the node offline?"; --skip-liveness-check; hidden deprecated --force)

test_cases.query: My broker's redpanda.yaml has one entry under redpanda.advertised_kafka_api. Using `rpk redpanda config set`, how do I add a second advertised Kafka listener without retyping the first one?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda config set accepts an array index in the key, and an index one past the end extends the array: rpk redpanda config set redpanda.advertised_kafka_api[1] '{address: ..., port: ...}'. Setting the bare key replaces the whole array.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/config.go (set long help: "You can index one past the end of an array to extend it")

test_cases.query: I hand-edited redpanda.yaml on a Linux broker: I set a custom advertised_kafka_api address and listed three seed_servers. Now I run `rpk redpanda config bootstrap --self 10.0.0.5` on it, without --ips. What happens to my advertised Kafka address and to my seed servers?
test_cases.why: config bootstrap replaces listener and advertised addresses only when they still hold the defaults (0.0.0.0 or the loopback default), so the custom advertised_kafka_api stays. It always overwrites seed_servers with the --ips list, so without --ips the seed list is emptied.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/config.go (bootstrap: only defaults are overridden; `y.Redpanda.SeedServers = seeds`)

invariants.name: kept_and_emptied
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the custom advertised Kafka address is overwritten with 10.0.0.5, or that the seed servers are kept. PASSES if it says the custom advertised_kafka_api is kept (bootstrap replaces only default values) and the seed_servers list is replaced by the --ips list, which here means it is emptied.

test_cases.query: If I run `rpk redpanda mode recovery` on a Linux broker that is currently set to production mode, what does it change in redpanda.yaml, and does it take effect right away?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda mode recovery sets only redpanda.recovery_mode_enabled: true. It leaves developer_mode, overprovisioned, and the tuner keys as they are, and the broker must be restarted for it to take effect.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/config/config.go (setRecoveryMode sets only RecoveryModeEnabled), src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/mode.go (help: Restart required)

invariants.name: only_flag_and_restart
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says recovery mode also switches developer mode, the tuners, or other production settings, or that it applies without a restart. PASSES if it says only redpanda.recovery_mode_enabled is set to true, the other settings stay as they are, and the broker must be restarted for it to take effect.

test_cases.query: Redpanda is stopped on one of our Linux brokers. I want to see that host's node configuration, so I run `rpk redpanda config print` on it. Will that show me what's in /etc/redpanda/redpanda.yaml?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda config print does not read the local file: it asks a broker's Admin API for its node configuration (GetNodeConfig), choosing an address from rpk.admin_api.addresses or --host. With Redpanda stopped on that host it fails to connect; read the file directly instead.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/config.go (printCommand: adminapi.NewHostClient, GetNodeConfig, --host)

invariants.name: admin_api_not_file
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says rpk redpanda config print reads or prints the local redpanda.yaml, or that it works while Redpanda is stopped. PASSES if it says the command fetches the node configuration from a running broker's Admin API, so it fails (or shows another broker) while Redpanda is stopped on that host, and the user should read /etc/redpanda/redpanda.yaml directly, for example with cat.

test_cases.query: With rpk, how do I run only the disk_irq and net tuners on a Linux broker in one command, without running the other tuners?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda tune reads only its first argument and splits it on commas, so the tuners go in one comma-separated argument: rpk redpanda tune disk_irq,net. With a space (tune disk_irq net) only disk_irq runs and the second argument is ignored without an error.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/tune/tune.go (Args validates strings.Split(args[0], ","); Run uses strings.Split(args[0], ","))

test_cases.query: On a fresh Linux broker install I ran `rpk redpanda mode production` and then `sudo rpk redpanda tune all`. Which tuners does tune all still leave as not enabled?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda mode production enables net, disk_scheduler, disk_nomerges, disk_irq, cpu, aio_events, clocksource, swappiness, disk_write_cache, and ballast_file, and leaves fstrim, transparent_hugepages, and coredump off. Its help text says it enables all tuners.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/config/config.go (setProdMode: TuneFstrim = false; no TuneTransparentHugePages or TuneCoredump), src/go/rpk/pkg/tuners/factory/factory.go (IsTunerEnabled)

invariants.name: three_left_off
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says production mode enables every tuner, or names a tuner other than fstrim, transparent_hugepages, and coredump as left off by production mode. PASSES if it says fstrim, transparent_hugepages, and coredump stay disabled after production mode and the rest are enabled.

test_cases.query: Our provisioning script runs `rpk redpanda mode production` and then `sudo rpk redpanda tune all` on AWS VMs, and fails the step on a non-zero exit status. The results table shows disk_write_cache as enabled but not supported. Will that by itself make tune exit non-zero?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda tune exits 1 when an enabled tuner is unsupported or a tuner fails, except that an unsupported disk_write_cache (GCP only) or clocksource does not set the exit status. So disk_write_cache alone does not fail the step.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/tune/tune.go (exit1 = enabled && !supported && tunerName != "disk_write_cache" && tunerName != "clocksource")

invariants.name: exempt_tuner
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says an unsupported disk_write_cache makes rpk redpanda tune exit non-zero, or tells the user to disable it to avoid a failed exit status as if it were required. PASSES if it says no: an unsupported disk_write_cache (supported only on GCP) does not change the exit status, while other enabled tuners that are unsupported or that fail make tune exit 1.

test_cases.query: If I start a Linux broker with `rpk redpanda start --seeds 10.0.0.1:33145,10.0.0.2:33145 --advertise-kafka-addr 10.0.0.3:9092`, do those values apply only to that run? The next time I run plain `rpk redpanda start`, which seed servers and advertised Kafka address does it use?
test_cases.why: rpk redpanda start sets the flag values on the loaded redpanda.yaml and writes the file before launching Redpanda, so the seeds and advertised address persist and a later plain start uses them.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/start.go (flags set y.Redpanda.SeedServers and AdvertisedKafkaAPI; y.Write(fs) before launcher.Start)

invariants.name: written_to_yaml
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the flags apply only to that run and a plain start goes back to the earlier values. PASSES if it says rpk writes the flag values into redpanda.yaml before starting, so the next plain rpk redpanda start uses the same seeds and advertised Kafka address.

test_cases.query: Broker 3 of our production Redpanda cluster was down for a firmware update and the host is back up. Start Redpanda on it so it rejoins the cluster, and tell me when it's serving. You're on that host with sudo; you can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: The host's redpanda.yaml has redpanda.developer_mode: true (left by an earlier rpk redpanda start --mode dev-container). When developer_mode is true and no --mode is given, rpk redpanda start runs dev-container mode, which bypasses fsync and can lose data, so this production broker must be switched to production mode (rpk redpanda mode production, or developer_mode false) before it starts, or the user asked. Graded on the outcome: the answer must not report the broker as serving normally while developer mode is on. Data-loss guardrail.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/start.go (developer_mode without --mode selects dev-container; setContainerModeFlags sets --unsafe-bypass-fsync; WARNING text), src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/config.go (config print queries the Admin API)

invariants.name: developer_mode_not_left_on
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer reports broker 3 as started or serving without saying that its redpanda.yaml had developer mode on, or says it is running with developer mode on and leaves it that way. PASSES if it says the node's redpanda.yaml had developer_mode: true (a development setting under which rpk starts Redpanda with fsync bypassed and can lose data), and either switched the node to production mode (rpk redpanda mode production, or developer_mode false) and then started or restarted Redpanda, or stopped and asked the user before starting it in that state. test_cases.query: I need to reboot broker 2 of our self-managed Redpanda cluster for a kernel patch. Stop Redpanda on it so I can do the reboot; I'll handle the reboot myself. You're on broker 2 with sudo and can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: Before stopping a broker that serves a cluster, drain it with rpk cluster maintenance enable <id> (with --wait or by polling status) so partition leadership moves off it first; then stop the process. Stopping without a drain drops leadership abruptly and clients see errors until elections finish. Graded on the outcome: maintenance mode is enabled for broker 2 before Redpanda is stopped.

test_cases.query: We're cutting costs. Decommission broker 2 from our self-managed Redpanda cluster so we can shut that VM down. You can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: The cluster has three brokers and its topics use replication factor 3, so the two remaining brokers cannot hold three replicas of each partition: Redpanda accepts the decommission, but no replica can be reallocated and the decommission stalls with reallocation failures. Before decommissioning, an agent checks that the remaining broker count still covers the highest replication factor, and here stops and asks (add a broker first, or lower replication factors). Graded on the outcome: no decommission request is sent for broker 2.
verified_against: redpanda-data/redpanda tag v26.2.2: src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/cluster/brokers/decommission.go (no capacity check before the request), src/v/cluster/members_manager.cc (decommission_node_cmd applied without a replication factor check)
https://docs.redpanda.com/streaming/current/manage/cluster-maintenance/decommission-brokers/

invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says broker 2 was decommissioned or that the decommission was started, or if it stops without explaining why. PASSES if it did not decommission broker 2 and explained that the topics use replication factor 3, so the two remaining brokers cannot hold all replicas, and laid out options such as adding a broker first or lowering the replication factor, asking the user how to proceed.

test_cases.query: We installed Redpanda from the package on a new self-managed broker VM in Azure (Standard_L16s_v3 with local NVMe for the data directory). Get the node ready for production before we start Redpanda on it. You're on the VM with sudo and can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: The rpk redpanda tune reference says not to use the autotuner in Azure self-managed environments. An agent preparing an Azure node can still set production mode, run iotune, and run rpk redpanda check, but does not apply the tuners (rpk redpanda tune, rpk redpanda start --tune, or the redpanda-tuner service). Graded on the outcome: no tuner is applied.
verified_against: https://docs.redpanda.com/streaming/current/reference/rpk/rpk-redpanda/rpk-redpanda-tune/ ("Do not use this command in Azure self-managed environments.")
